title: Characterization of Respiratory Syncytial Virus Matrix Mutants with Cryo-Electron Tomography and Sub-Tomogram Averaging
content: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is an enveloped, negative sense-RNA virus that assembles into pleomorphic, filamentous particles [1, 2]. Clinical manifestation varies from person to person; however, infants, immunocompromised individuals, and the elderly are at higher risk of developing more severe disease upon infection with RSV [3]. While in recent years, vaccines have been developed for adults over 75 years of age and pregnant woman, development of antivirals and vaccines for infants remain an unmet need [4]. Furthering our understanding of how RSV replicates, particularly its virion structure, could reveal novel targets for vaccine and antiviral development.
